thread:
alex: Heads-up — prod-eu NAT gateway is hitting ephemeral port limits, 3/3 gateways ~100% used, a bunch of outbound calls failing :grimacing:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: NAT-GW-EphemeralPort > 95% for prod-eu-west-1. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod-eu/d/egress/nat-gateway (sig: high)
priya: On it. Any idea which service/traffic pattern is causing the churn?
alex: Correlates with inference-worker fleet. We see lots of short-lived HTTPS calls to model-registry and S3 for model shards — sidecar per pod is making outbound TLS per request (no keepalive).
jordan: Can you paste a quick netstat from a node in that subnet?
alex: ```
$ sudo netstat -an | grep ':443' | awk '{print $6}' | sort | uniq -c
  15000 TIME_WAIT
   4000 ESTABLISHED
   2000 CLOSE_WAIT
```
alex: On the node nat-trace we saw ~62k ephemeral ports allocated (close to 65535 range).
sam: If each request does a new TCP handshake, TIME_WAIT accumulates and NAT mapping consumes ports. Sidecars that don't reuse keep-alive will burn ephemeral ports fast.
priya: Sidecar image: registry.redwood/egress-proxy:v1.8.2 — we rolled it two days ago as part of the fleet update.
jordan: Quick mitigations we can do now: 1) Add an extra NAT gateway in the affected AZs (split subnets), 2) Route some subnets through a spare NAT, 3) If possible, add an internal egress proxy that pools TLS connections.
priya: I'll provision an additional NAT GW (prod-eu-nat-4) and update the private route tables for two subnets to split the load. Starting now, ETA ~15m.
alex: Good. Also we should patch the sidecar to enable HTTP keepalive and connection reuse. That will drastically reduce new sockets.
priya: Done — route table update pushed. Monitoring shows ephemeral usage dropping from ~98% -> ~62% after switching two subnets to prod-eu-nat-4. :thumbsup:
monitoring-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: NAT-GW-EphemeralPort back under 85% in prod-eu-west-1.
sam: Next steps (post-incident):
- Add infra runbook for NAT GW autoscale (pre-provision extra NATs for bursty workloads)
- Add an egress proxy pattern for model pulls (pool TLS)
- Fix sidecar: enable connection keepalive + reuse dialer, ensure HTTP2 where possible
- Add a synthetic test to measure ephemeral port churn per request profile
jordan: I'll open INFRA-3421 with the config recommendations + runbook and link the roll plan.
priya: Added ticket INFRA-3421 and attached graphs and the route change steps: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3421
alex: Thanks all. Long-term: we should consider moving bulk model pulls to a cached puller inside the node (single long-lived connection) or use a shared egress proxy per AZ.
sam: Agreed. Also let's add a quick note to the deployment checklist: "avoid short-lived outbound connections for high-cardinality traffic".
priya: I'll run a small load test tomorrow to validate the keepalive patch and quantify port savings. :eyes:
alex: Closing thread for now, keeping monitoring alerts open for 24h.
